newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INJURED TAYLOR IN DOUBT FOR SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INJURED TAYLOR IN DOUBT FOR SECOND TEST.

text.p: Australian captain Mark Taylor has suffered yet another back injury and could be in danger of missing the second test against South Africa starting in Port Elizabeth next Friday.

"Mark felt some pain in the lower right side of his back. At this stage we are evaluating the signs and symptoms and seeing how he responds to treatment," physiotherapist Errol Alcott said before the start of Australia's three-day match against Border.
"At least it is on the opposite side to where he had surgery last year. He may need a scan if it doesn't improve but at this stage we don't know much apart from what he feels...pain.

"It might be related to his serious injury of last year because it is on the same level -- fifth lumbar and first sacrum -- but we won't know until we can have a look inside. The pain is nowhere near as intense as it was before he had surgery but he is understandably cautious. We can only hope it's not too serious."
Australia beat South Africa by an innings and 195 runs in the first test in Johannesburg.
